title: fix(objectql)!: a select refuses a plain object or an array as its value, and as a multi-value element (#29244)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9BsrKH5NsKzU1otmTa7SMs8)_
Fixes #29244

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no file under `skills/**` or `content/docs/**` teaches writing an object or an array into a `select` (a `git grep` of `skills/**` for select values shows only option-code examples); the data skill already authors a select's value as an option `value`.

Clause-② measured on `origin/main` @ `04e0c2c0` (base) and on this branch (head): writes the base admitted are now refused (table under Why). Metadata-protocol stays `none`: no key, value or metadata type an author writes moves; the narrowed face is a data write's answer.

> **BREAKING** for a data write that sends an object or an array where a select expects an option value. FROM: `{ stage: { a: 1 } }` or `{ stage: ["x"] }` on a single-value `select` / `radio` with no `options` answered `201` / `200` and stored the object or the array (SQLite as its JSON text); so did `{ stage: ["a"] }` on a select whose options include `a`, and `{ labels: [{ a: 1 }] }` or `{ labels: [["a"]] }` on a `multiple: true` select, `multiselect`, `checkboxes` or `tags` field. TO: each is refused `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` with the field's `invalid_type`, and nothing is stored. The fix for a caller: send the option code itself (`{ stage: "x" }`), or an array of codes on a multi-value field; structured data belongs in a `json` field.

**Landing hold.** Seat 3's PR #29464 (same file, the blank path) lands first, per ruling #29346 B execution step 3. It is still a draft as this PR opens, so this PR is a draft too; it merges `origin/main` after #29464 lands and checks `merge-tree` is clean then. The two do not overlap: this diff does not touch `normalizeBlankTypedValues`, the blank/`''` arm or the `BOUNDED_STRING_FIELD_TYPES` string arm.

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:`select` / `radio` 单值字段收到对象或数组时,服务端写入口改为拒收(400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`,字段码 `invalid_type`),有无 `options` 都一样;多值选项字段(`multiple: true` 的 select、multiselect、checkboxes、tags)数组里夹着对象或嵌套数组的元素也拒收。
- **为什么改**:没声明 `options` 的自由选择字段原样把 `{a:1}`、`["x"]` 交给驱动存下,有选项的字段也因为 `String(["a"])` 等于 `"a"` 而把数组存进去;列表、筛选(筛选入口本来就拒收这种比较值)和报表都读不了这种值。
- **风险与回滚**:以前写得进去的对象/数组写入现在被拒;普查(objectql、rest、runtime、自动化流程、dogfood 全套,含示例应用种子数据)没有一个产品写入方这样写。已存的旧值不改写、不迁移。回滚 = revert 本 PR。
- **先看**:`packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts` 的 select/radio 单值分支与多值选项分支新增的形状检查;`packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.select-shape.test.ts`;`.changeset/29244-select-object-array-value.md`。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest exec vitest run src/rest-data-select-shape.test.ts`,预期 7 个测试全绿(主干上 6 个红:POST 201、PATCH 200 并把对象/数组存进库)。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位落地(须等 #29464 先合并)。

## What changes

- **Single-value arm** (`select` / `radio` when not multi-valued, `record-validator.ts`): a plain object or an array is refused `invalid_type` with the ADR-0104 `invalid_value_shape` sentence ("expected one option value, received an object" / "an array"). It is a shape test, so it runs ahead of `shapeOnly` (a readonly value is reached, as the string arm's #29133 rule is) and ahead of option membership. The #5922 operator-object check still runs first and keeps its own sentence.
- **Multi-value option branch** (`multiple: true` select/radio, `multiselect`, `checkboxes`, `tags`): an element that is a plain object or an array is refused `invalid_type` ("expected an array of option values, received an element that is an object" / "an array"), again ahead of `shapeOnly` and membership. An array of strings, numbers or booleans is judged as before; a value that is not an array keeps its existing `invalid_type_array` sentence; a lone scalar is still wrapped by the engine.
- **The spec's contract.** `valueSchemaFor` (`packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts`) already says an option field's stored element is a declared code or, with no `options`, a string. This makes the write door agree for the two shapes the card names; it does not touch `packages/spec`.
- **No new code or sentence.** `invalid_type` and the `invalid_value_shape` catalog entry are the ones the string arm and the operator rule already use.
- **Scope note (declared, bounded in-place).** The card names the free-form single select and asks for a decision on `multiple: true`. The same arm admitted `["a"]` on a select with declared options (by its string reading), and the same multi-value branch admitted object elements on `multiselect` / `checkboxes` / `tags`. Both are the same defect class in the same branch, closed by the same mechanical rule with the same gates, so they are fixed here rather than as a type-by-type split (one rule per branch, not per type). Raised in the report for the seat.

## Why

Measured with a recording driver behind the real engine (insert, update by id, update by predicate: all three doors answer the same in every row) and through the real REST routes on SQLite and driver-memory (POST create, PATCH update):

| Field | Value | base | head |
|---|---|---|---|
| `select`, no options (and `radio`) | `{ a: 1 }` | ADMIT, driver got `{"a":1}`; REST 201/200, read back the object (SQLite: its JSON text) | 400 `invalid_type` |
| `select`, no options (and `radio`) | `["x"]`, `[]` | ADMIT, driver got the array | 400 `invalid_type` |
| `select`, options `a`/`b` | `["a"]` | ADMIT, driver got `["a"]`; REST 201, read back `["a"]` | 400 `invalid_type` |
| `select`, options `a`/`b` | `{ a: 1 }` | 400 `invalid_option` | 400 `invalid_type` (code moves) |
| `select` `multiple: true`, no options | `[{ a: 1 }]`, `[["x"]]` | ADMIT, stored | 400 `invalid_type` |
| `select` `multiple: true`, options `a`/`b` | `[["a"]]` | ADMIT, stored | 400 `invalid_type` |
| `multiselect` / `tags` / `checkboxes`, free | `[{ a: 1 }]`, `[["x"]]` | ADMIT | 400 `invalid_type` |
| controls | `"x"`, `3`, `"a"`, `["x","y"]`, lone `"x"` on multi | ADMIT (as before) | ADMIT (as before) |

**Writer census** (who writes an object or an array into a select today). A log-only probe in the select arms of `origin/main` @ `04e0c2c0`, built into objectql's `dist/`, recorded every object/array value while these suites ran: `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation` (flow nodes, including `create_record` / `update_record` and the screen paths) and the dogfood battery (which boots the example apps, `packages/apps`, the platform objects and their seeds). Positive control: the probe recorded the 36 writes of a one-off REST probe that reaches objectql through `dist/`, and the objectql probe's own writes.

| Writer | Hits |
|---|---|
| Seeds and data in `examples/`, `packages/apps`, platform objects (dogfood, runtime) | 0 |
| Flow / screen paths (`service-automation`, dogfood flow fixtures) | 0 |
| Dogfood fixtures | 0 |
| Tests | 2: the two #5922 pins re-homed below |

Not exhaustive: plugin suites and other service packages were not run under the probe.

**`unique` and filters.** A `unique` free-form select (REST, SQLite and driver-memory): base admitted `{a:1}` then `{a:1}` as 201, 409 and `{a:1}` then `{a:2}` as 201, 201; head refuses each write 400 before the unique check. `"x"` then `"x"` is 201, 409 on both. Filters do not move: the filter door already refused an object or array comparand on a select (`engine.find` `INVALID_FILTER`, `GET` 400) on base and head, and `{ free: "x" }` / `{ free: { $in: ["x"] } }` answer the same rows on both.

## Tests

New files:

- `packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.select-shape.test.ts`: single-value `select` (free and declared) and `radio` refuse object, `{}`, array and `[]` on insert and update with the shape detail; the message names field, type and shape; a readonly select is reached; an operator object keeps its own sentence; every multi-value option type refuses an object element and an array element; controls (scalars, arrays of scalars, membership, non-array sentence, null); end to end through the engine's insert, update by id and update by predicate with a recording driver that sees no write, and a scalar / array / wrapped lone scalar that still land.
- `packages/rest/src/rest-data-select-shape.test.ts` (7 tests): real `ObjectQL` + SQLite `SqlDriver` + `RestServer`: POST and PATCH with `{a:1}`, `["x"]` on a free select and `[{a:1}]` on a `multiple: true` select answer 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` / `invalid_type`, no row is written and the PATCHed row is unchanged (physical row read); control stores a string and an array of strings.

Forced edits to existing tests:

- `packages/objectql/src/validation/operator-object-write-value.test.ts`: `admits an UNDECLARED $-spelling` and `admits a plain non-operator object` (on `stage_free`, moved there by #29223) rested on exactly this admission. Restated as refusals that assert the SHAPE sentence and that the message does not name a filter operator: that is what the pins prove (the operator rule did not claim `$inn` or `{a:1}`). Moving them to `json` would pin nothing, because a `json` column skips the operator rule entirely, and no scalar-valued type is left that admits a plain object.

<details><summary>Ablations</summary>

Made with `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit once, blob moved), objectql rebuilt with `--force`, marker proven in dist by `scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` ("marker present in 4 built files"), each restored by the tool (blob == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty), then a final rebuild with the marker absent from all 14 built files and both files green (69/69, 7/7).

| Ablation | Red |
|---|---|
| A: the single-value shape test off | unit `Tests 29 failed \| 40 passed (69)` (every single-value refusal, both restated #5922 pins); REST `Tests 4 failed \| 3 passed (7)` (the four `stage` cases) |
| B: the element test off | unit `Tests 11 failed \| 58 passed (69)` (every element case, the end-to-end refusal); REST `Tests 2 failed \| 5 passed (7)` (the two `labels` cases) |

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **A number on a single-value select** (`{ stage: 3 }`) is still admitted and stored as the number, although the spec's stored element is a string. Out of this card (the card names objects and arrays); the same normalisation #29241 did for the text family would be its own card.
- **Rows already stored** with an object or array value are not rewritten or re-judged; the `os migrate value-shapes` scan does not cover option fields.
- **Not measured:** PostgreSQL, MySQL (same knex path), MongoDB (no daemon in the container).

## Verification

Head `3ffa21c9`, branched from `origin/main` @ `04e0c2c0`. `origin/main` has moved since (to `390bd2ae`, no commit touching the five files here, `git merge-tree` clean); per the card delta this branch merges `origin/main` once #29464 lands, and the suites are re-run on that head then. CI runs the rest: see the PR's check-runs.

| objectql full suite (`vitest run --maxWorkers=2`) | Test Files 536 passed (536) · Tests 10432 passed (10432) |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest typecheck` | exit 0 |
| rest full suite | Test Files 379 passed (379) · Tests 7352 passed, 352 skipped (7704) |
| dogfood battery (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test`, a narrowing) | Test Files 397 passed, 3 skipped (400) · Tests 3277 passed, 28 skipped (3305) |
| `eslint --no-inline-config packages/objectql packages/rest` | exit 0 |
| `dispatch-gates --commands` (61 derived), reconciled with `--ran` | 61 derived, 61 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN; all exit 0 |

`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:type-check-debt` first answered exit 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: seven packages outside the closure had no `dist/`, and the dogfood closure build was in flight); after building those seven, both exit 0. The plugin-teardown self-test needed `git fetch --depth 1 origin 621a4876…`.

The census runs (base + probe) built with `OS_SKIP_DTS=1`, so their dogfood leg also showed 6 reds in `rest-route-generation-tombstones.test.ts` (TS7016, no `.d.ts` for `@objectstack/spec/api`): a build-mode artifact of that run only; the head battery above, on a full-declaration build, is green.
